item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-10
item.description: On 2026-11-08 the Europe–China Digital Commons Observatory published an OCR pass over OpenAtom Open Source Foundation's statutory annual work reports to the Ministry of Civil Affairs for 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 — and the figures it recovered, labelled evidence A, do not line up with the numbers the foundation's own conference keynotes use. Filed income 2020–2023 is ¥270.5 million, of which ¥223.6 million is donations; ¥23.6 million is government subsidy, concentrated in a single ¥20.7 million item in 2023 restricted to an ecosystem-cultivation platform. Foreign donations are zero in all four years. In 2023, Huawei Device and Huawei Technologies together gave ¥27.85 million — 37 percent of that year's ¥75.5 million donation base — while the foundation paid ¥6.49 million to Huawei Cloud and ¥1.65 million more for OpenHarmony code hosting. On 2026-08-28 the same foundation committed ¥150 million a year for three years in a keynote. Its disclosure page, checked directly for this briefing, still lists four reports, 2020 through 2023. Today's entry reads those filings for what they say about who funds a Chinese open-source foundation and what the money is classified as, then uses the observatory's companion pass over 34 EU and Chinese projects to ask the question the filings are now precise enough to ask: whether the distinguishing feature of Chinese public funding for open source is its size, or the line it is booked under.
